findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update compares org-aware (wrapped) original against raw updated model, missing invalidations
findings.body: In update(), the "original" IdP passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is obtained via getById(...), which wraps the model with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel when the organization feature is enabled. That wrapper overrides isEnabled() to additionally require the linked organization to be enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate then evaluates LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() (which includes isEnabled()) on this wrapped original but on the raw updated model, so the two sides are not comparable — and neither matches what defines cache membership, since the cached login lists are filled by idpDelegate.getForLogin(...), which filters on the raw persisted enabled flag. When the IdP's organization is currently disabled, the predicate on the wrapped original is always false, so any update that also makes the raw updated model fail the predicate registers no invalidation. Concretely: disable an org whose public IdP is already in the cached getForLogin lists, then set hideOnLogin=true (or linkOnly=true, or brokerPublic=false) on that IdP — original predicate is false (org disabled) and updated predicate is false, so no login-cache invalidation is registered. When the org is re-enabled (org changes do not invalidate these caches), getForLogin still returns the stale cached entry, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean — which only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin/linkOnly/brokerPublic — renders the IdP on the login page even though the administrator explicitly removed it from login. Fix by basing the invalidation decision on the raw stored model (e.g. idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())) instead of the org-aware wrapper, or by invalidating the login caches unconditionally on update.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin cleanup targets literal alias "alias", leaking all created identity providers
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup is registered as getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) — the literal string "alias" instead of the alias of the provider just created ("idp-alias-" + i in the loop at line 381, and "idp-alias-20" at line 425). Consequently none of the 21 identity providers created by this test are removed afterwards; each cleanup targets a nonexistent provider named "alias" (a silent 404). The leftover brokers remain in the shared test realm and can pollute subsequent tests that count identity providers or render the login page. Register the cleanup with the actual alias, e.g. capture final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; and use testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove.
